The following provides a quick overview of the main components and their interactions.

**`Main`** (consisting of classes [`Main`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W09-3/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/Main.java) and [`MainApp`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W09-3/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/MainApp.java)) is in charge of the app launch and shut down.
* At app launch, it initializes the other components in the correct sequence, and connects them up with each other.
* At shut down, it shuts down the other components and invokes cleanup methods where necessary.
The bulk of the app's work is done by the following four components:
* [**`UI`**](#ui-component): Accepts commands and displays client lists, profiles and feedback.
* [**`Logic`**](#logic-component): Interprets commands and coordinates data changes, saving and session history.
* [**`Model`**](#model-component): Holds client data, the active list view and undo/redo state in memory.
* [**`Storage`**](#storage-component): Loads and saves client data and preferences in local JSON files.
[**`Commons`**](#common-classes) provides shared utilities. Its individual dependencies
are omitted from the overview to avoid clutter; it is not a separate step in command execution.

The menu bar provides `File` and `Help` actions, plus an `Edit` menu for `Undo`, `Redo` and `History`. The `Edit` actions submit the corresponding commands through `CommandBox`, so they use the same execution path and show feedback in `ResultDisplay` just like typed commands. Undo also has `Ctrl+Z` on Windows and Linux or `Cmd+Z` on macOS; redo has `Ctrl+Y` or `Cmd+Shift+Z`, respectively. These shortcuts work while the command box has focus. Menu actions and shortcuts do not submit unfinished command-box text, so a failed action leaves that text unchanged and does not give it the error style. The error style is applied only when a command submitted with Enter fails.
`Logic#canUndo()` and `Logic#canRedo()` expose the model's history availability to

available even when both stacks are empty.
The scene-level history key filter runs before the command text field can handle
its own text undo. It consumes a recognized history shortcut even when the
corresponding menu item is disabled, so the app reports an unavailable action
instead of editing the user's draft. `MainWindowTest` covers this routing,
draft preservation, input styling and menu state.

A client's role is a dedicated `ClientRole` field on `Person`, not a tag. `ClientRole` is an enum with exactly three declared values, and each value carries two strings: the token the user types and the data file stores, and the text the interface shows.

The command token `none` is not an enum value, and the app never writes it to the data file. It clears the optional field, so the `role` key is omitted when the client book is saved. Undo and redo treat this as an ordinary role change.
| Stored token | Shown to the user |

`ClientRole#getValue()` returns the stored token, `ClientRole#getDisplayValue()` returns the text shown, and `ClientRole#toString()` returns the display value, so a role cannot be shown one way in the result message and another way on the client's badge.

**Saving and reading back.** `JsonAdaptedPerson` mirrors the model field as a string. When a client book is saved the role is written with `ClientRole#getValue()`, and because the field carries `@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)`, a client with no role leaves the `role` key out of the data file entirely. When a client book is read back, a missing key, a blank value or `none` (ignoring case) becomes no role, so a hand-edited file can write `"role": "none"` where the app would leave the key out. Any other value goes through `ClientRole#fromString(String)`; an unrecognised token raises an `IllegalValueException` carrying `Invalid Role: Role must be 'buyer', 'seller', or 'both'.`. A typo in a hand-edited data file is therefore reported rather than silently ignored.
**Why a dedicated field and not a tag.** Tags allow arbitrary alphanumeric labels and
multiple values; they do not enforce the role vocabulary. A dedicated optional enum restricts
a client to one role value, with `BOTH` representing the combined buyer/seller relationship.
An absent role is represented by null independently of unrelated tags. `Person` compares
roles with `Objects.equals`, so absence is a supported state. Tags could encode roles only
with additional conventions and validation that the dedicated field already supplies.

**Client books with no role.** A client book written before the role existed has no `role` key, and every record in it loads with no role assigned. The sample clients shipped with the app set roles so that the feature is visible on first run, and the model class diagram above shows `ClientRole` as an optional association of `Person`. The saving and reading path, `JsonAddressBookStorage` to `JsonSerializableAddressBook` to `JsonAdaptedPerson`, is unchanged and is shown in `StorageClassDiagram.puml`.

A note is free-text working detail kept on a client: where a negotiation stands, when to call back, what to prepare for a viewing. It holds 1 to 500 characters after surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and it may contain real line breaks.

**Parsing.** `NoteCommandParser` splits the index from the note text, and the text runs to the end of the line, so it may contain spaces. The parser delegates ordinary note text to `ParserUtil#parseNote`, which scans it once from left to right: `\n` becomes a real line break, `\\` becomes a literal backslash, and an unrecognised or trailing backslash is preserved. This makes `\\n` an escaped backslash followed by `n`, so users can store a literal `\n` in paths and other text. The decoded result is trimmed of surrounding whitespace and handed to `Note` for validation. The lowercase word `clear` is reserved after trimming surrounding whitespace: only `clear` clears the note, while `CLEAR` and sentences such as `Please clear the outstanding paperwork` are stored as ordinary text. A blank note or one longer than 500 decoded characters raises a `ParseException` carrying `Notes should be 1 to 500 characters.`

**Executing.** `NoteCommand` builds a new `Person` that carries the new note, or no note for the clear form, and copies every other field from the client being edited, then calls `Model#setPerson`. It does not touch the filtered list, so an active search or filter stays in effect. The result message is `Note updated for <name>.` or `Note cleared for <name>.`

**Storing.** `JsonAdaptedPerson` mirrors the note as a string under the `note` key. Because the field carries `@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)`, a client with no note leaves the key out of the data file entirely. A real line break in the model value is represented by the escaped characters `\n` in the JSON file and is decoded back into a line break when the file is read. A missing key becomes no note, and a value that is blank or longer than 500 characters raises an `IllegalValueException` carrying the same message, so a hand-edited data file is reported rather than silently accepted. A 500-character two-line note therefore survives a restart unchanged.

**Display.** `DetailPane` displays the selected client's note in its existing note row, with wrapping and preserved line breaks. The row is hidden when no note exists, and the profile scrolls vertically when needed. `NoteCommand` returns the updated client's index when that client remains in the filtered list, so the UI selects the replacement `Person` and refreshes the profile. See [Detailed client view](#detailed-client-view) for the selection rules.

**Why `find` does not search notes.** `find` matches name, phone number, email and address. Notes contain free-text working details, so searching them could return unrelated clients. Users can read a note in the detail panel and replace it with `note`.

**Why `find` requires every keyword.** `PersonMatchesSearchTermsPredicate` tests that every keyword is contained in the client's name, phone number, email address or address, and a keyword may be matched by a different field from another keyword. An agent adds a keyword to make a search more specific, so `find Alex Yu` must not show everyone named Alex or Yu. Matching any keyword was considered, as in AB3, but it made the list grow as the agent typed more, and a quoted phrase would not help the agent who types the words without quotes. The cost is that one search can no longer find two different clients by their names, so the agent runs two searches.

**Why `find` searches the address.** An agent often remembers where a client lives or wants to buy but not their name, and the address is already stored in the client record. `PersonMatchesSearchTermsPredicate#test` therefore treats the address as a fourth field, with the same case-insensitive substring rule as the other three, so the agent has no extra prefix to learn and `find Bishan` works the same way as `find Alicia`. The preferred areas (`l/`) and the tags are not searched, because `filter l/` and `filter t/` already cover them with exact values, and a keyword that is a block number or a word such as `Street` can now match many clients, as a short name keyword already could. With no keywords, the predicate never matches, but `FindCommandParser` rejects that input first.

### Compact client cards and filter status

use ellipses, while the index and role badge keep their preferred widths.
Absent role badges, note markers and requirements are both invisible and

**Tag overflow.** `PersonCard` sorts the tags before passing them to `TagRow`,
which fits whole labels into the available width, reserving room for a `+N`

and uses the labels' computed widths

`clear` deletes every client, so it needs two steps. `clear` warns and starts a pending state, and `clear confirm` completes it. Any other input cancels it.

**Parsing.** `ClearCommandParser` accepts no argument or `confirm` in any letter case, after trimming, and creates `ClearCommand(isConfirmed)` with the flag set only for `confirm`. Any other argument raises a `ParseException` with `Invalid command format. Use: clear.`.
**Executing.** `ClearCommand#execute(Model)` counts the clients in the whole address book, not the filtered list, because clear also deletes hidden clients. It then does one of three things:
| The address book is empty | `The client book is already empty.` and nothing is pending |

| Not confirmed | `This will delete the only client. Type clear confirm to proceed.` for one client, or `This will delete all N clients. Type clear confirm to proceed.`, with `CommandResult#isAwaitingConfirmation()` set |
| Confirmed | Replaces the address book with an empty one and shows `Client book has been cleared!` |

**Remembering the pending state.** `LogicManager` holds one `isClearPending` flag. It is set from `CommandResult#isAwaitingConfirmation()` only after the command has run and any changed data has been saved, so a failed save never leaves a clear pending. **Parsing.** `FilterCommandParser` tokenizes the arguments with `PREFIX_ROLE`, `PREFIX_TAG`, `PREFIX_AREA`, `PREFIX_HOUSING_TYPE`, `PREFIX_BUDGET` and `PREFIX_ASKING_PRICE`. It rejects any text before the first prefix and rejects a second `r/`, `b/` or `s/`. The role is parsed with `ClientRole.fromString` after trimming it, the tags with `ParserUtil#parseTags`, the areas with `ParserUtil#parseAreas` and the housing types with `ParserUtil#parseHousingTypes`. The budget and the asking price go through `ParserUtil#parsePriceRange`, which reads either one price or `MIN-MAX` using `ParserUtil#parsePrice`, so prices follow the same rules as in `add`, and rejects a range that is not two prices joined by a hyphen, such as `500000-`, with `PriceRange.MESSAGE_INVALID_FORMAT`, and a minimum above the maximum with `PriceRange.MESSAGE_REVERSED_RANGE`, which names the field (`budget` or `asking price`) like the other messages do. Every part is optional. The parser collects the parts that were given with `PersonMatchesFilterPredicate.Builder` and creates `FilterCommand` with the predicate that `build()` returns.

**The predicate.** `PersonMatchesFilterPredicate#test` is true only when every part matches. The constructor is private, because six mostly empty arguments are easy to mix up, so callers use the builder and leave unused parts out:

* **Role.** An omitted role criterion imposes no restriction. `buyer` matches `BUYER` and `BOTH`, `seller` matches `SELLER` and `BOTH`, and `both` matches only `BOTH`. A client with no role never matches a given role criterion.

* **Tags.** An omitted tag criterion imposes no restriction. Otherwise, one matching tag is enough, and tag names are compared ignoring case. A client with no tags cannot match a supplied tag criterion.

* **Areas and housing types.** These work like tags. An omitted criterion imposes no restriction; otherwise, one matching value is enough. A client with no recorded values cannot match a supplied criterion.

* **Budget.** A client matches when the budget range overlaps the filter's range, with both ends included, so `PriceRange#overlaps` checks `filterMin <= budgetMax && budgetMin <= filterMax`. A single price is a range with the same minimum and maximum, so it matches every budget that includes it. A client without a budget never matches.

* **Asking price.** A client matches when the asking price is inside the filter's range, with both ends included, as checked by `PriceRange#contains`. A single price therefore matches only that exact price. A client without an asking price never matches.
So different parts combine with AND, and the values within the tags, the areas and the housing types with OR.

`PriceRange` is a new immutable class in `seedu.address.model.person` that holds a minimum and a maximum `Price`, and it rejects a minimum above the maximum. It is separate from `Budget`, which describes what a client has recorded, because it is a query: it has a constructor for a single price, which is stored as a range with equal ends, and it knows how to compare itself with a `Budget` (`overlaps`) and with a `Price` (`contains`). 1. **Keyboard usability:** With the main window focused, an agent must be able to add, find, view,
update and delete clients, and request help, using the keyboard without a required mouse action.
Opening help with F1 or invoking undo/redo through a shortcut must preserve an unfinished
command draft. Viewing a client uses the typed `view INDEX` command or a mouse selection;
2. **Portability:** The same released JAR must launch and support the client-management workflow
on Windows 11, macOS and desktop Linux with Java 25, a working graphical environment and a
writable data directory. Each release must be smoke-tested on those OS families; a successful
test on one OS does not establish compatibility with another OS or CPU architecture.
3. **Responsiveness:** With 100 valid clients on a desktop with at least 4 GB of RAM and local SSD
storage, each warmed-up `list`, `find` and `filter` request should display its result within one
second. Measure five successive requests of each kind after one untimed warm-up request, with
no background build or test workload. Startup, external browser loading and slow/network storage
are excluded. This is a release-testing target, not a measured result or a 100-client input limit.
4. **Data integrity:** A successful data-changing request must remain intact after a normal restart.
A failed save must leave the previous saved file intact and restore the preceding in-memory
client data and undo/redo history. The application must not report success for an unsaved change.
An unreadable original file must remain recoverable rather than be silently overwritten; UC05
specifies the backup and startup-failure interaction.
5. **Robustness and error feedback:** Invalid commands, missing required arguments, invalid displayed
indexes and duplicate-contact conflicts must produce actionable feedback without terminating the
application or changing client data or undo/redo history. An operational save failure must report
the failure and leave the application available for a retry after the file-access problem is fixed.
6. **Layout accessibility:** At logical window sizes of 853 × 480 and 820 × 440, the command box,
feedback area, client list and detail panel must remain within the main window. A 500-character
note must wrap and be readable to its end using vertical scrolling. Actual Windows checks at
1920 × 1080 (100% and 125% scaling) and 1280 × 720 (150% scaling) must additionally verify that
controls and client details remain reachable. See [Testing](Testing.md#main-window-layout-checks)
for the distinction between logical-size tests and OS scaling tests.
7. **Maintainability:** On a documented development setup, `./gradlew check` must pass before a
release, including automated tests and configured style checks. Changes to parsing, client
updates or history/persistence behavior must have regression tests for the changed behavior.
This is a verification requirement, not a minimum coverage-percentage target.

EstateBookUltraProMax is a desktop client book for **property agents who manage
many buyers and sellers at once**. Type short commands to add, find and update
clients while the graphical interface keeps their contact details and property
requirements visible. This helps agents retrieve the right record during a call
or between viewings without searching through a spreadsheet.

* Command words are case-sensitive and must be lowercase. For example, use `list`, not `List` or `LIST`.
Parameter values ignore case only where their feature descriptions explicitly say so.
* An unknown command shows `Error: Unknown command. Type help for the User Guide link.`

* Words in `UPPER_CASE` are the parameters to be supplied by the user.
For example, in `add n/NAME`, replace `NAME` with a value such as `John Doe`.
* Items in square brackets are optional.
For example, `n/NAME [t/TAG]` can be used as `n/John Doe t/friend` or as `n/John Doe`.
* Items followed by `…`​ can appear zero or more times.
For example, `[t/TAG]…​` may be omitted, or written as `t/friend` or `t/friend t/family`.
* Prefixed fields in `add` and `edit` can appear in any order.
For example, if the command specifies `n/NAME p/PHONE_NUMBER`, `p/PHONE_NUMBER n/NAME` is also acceptable.
* Commands that take no parameters reject anything after the command word with `Invalid command format. Use: <command>.`

These rules apply when adding or editing clients.

| Name | Must start with a letter or number. Supports Unicode letters (including accented letters), combining marks, numbers, spaces, apostrophes (`'` and `’`), hyphens (`-`) and slashes (`/`), e.g. `Anne-Marie Tan`, `José Tan` and `Kumar s/o Ravi`. Extra spaces between words are reduced to one. |
| Phone | At least 3 digits; no spaces, letters or symbols. |
| Email | Use `local-part@domain`. See the email rules below. |

| Address | Cannot be blank. Free text, so the abbreviations `s/o` and `b/c` stay part of the address; a short word such as `s/ab` is read as an asking price and rejected, and so is `s/o,`, because an abbreviation must be a whole word. |
| Budget | Two whole-dollar amounts joined by a hyphen, such as `400000-600000`. Each amount is from 1 to 1,000,000,000, commas are optional, and the first amount cannot exceed the second. |
| Asking price | One whole-dollar amount from 1 to 1,000,000,000, with optional correctly placed commas. |
| Area | One of the 32 supported areas. Case is ignored and the standard spelling is stored, and extra spaces between words are reduced to one, so `l/Toa  Payoh` is stored as `Toa Payoh`. |
| Tag | Only English letters (`A–Z`, `a–z`) and digits (`0–9`) are allowed; no spaces or symbols. |

Prefixes are case-sensitive and must be lowercase, so `B/400000` is not read as a budget. A slash word that begins like a prefix but is not one, such as `bb/`, is reported as `Unknown prefix: bb/` rather than kept as text, and so is a prefix from another command, such as `r/`. The abbreviations `s/o` and `b/c` are kept as text in any letter case. A few address fragments that begin like a prefix, such as `Tel/Fax` or `nr/`, are reported the same way.
* Before `@`, use letters, digits and the symbols `+`, `_`, `.`, `-`.
* These symbols cannot appear at the start or end, or consecutively.
* Domain labels use letters, digits and internal hyphens (including consecutive hyphens), separated by dots.
The final label must have at least 2 characters.
* Each of `n/`, `p/`, `e/` and `a/` can appear only once per command.
* Repeat `t/` to supply multiple tags, such as `t/urgent t/firsttime`.
* Tags that differ only in letter case are treated as the same tag, so `t/urgent t/URGENT` stores one tag.
* For `edit`, use an empty `t/` to remove all tags.
The empty `t/` must be used alone for tags; do not combine it with another `t/`.
* Each of `b/` and `s/` can appear only once per command.
* Repeat `l/` to supply multiple areas, such as `l/Bedok l/Tampines`.
* Repeat `h/` to supply multiple housing types, such as `h/HDB h/Condo`.
* For `edit`, an empty `b/`, `s/`, `l/` or `h/` clears that field. In `add`, an empty prefix is an error.
An empty `l/` or `h/` must be used alone for that field; do not combine it with another `l/` or `h/`.

* Inside `n/NAME`, the whole relationship markers `s/o`, `d/o`, `a/l` and `a/p` are kept as part of the name, ignoring their capitalization. For example, `n/Kumar s/o Ravi s/950000` records the name `Kumar s/o Ravi` and an asking price of $950,000. Other field prefixes still end the name.

* If an address starts with `L` or `P` as a whole word (ignoring case), put the address before the name: `edit 1 a/P Ryan Road n/Bob`. Writing `edit 1 n/Bob a/P Ryan Road` instead stores `Bob a/P Ryan Road` as the name and leaves the address unchanged.
* Other slash text, such as `x/y`, is also valid in names: `n/Bob x/y` stores the name `Bob x/y`. Check field prefixes for typing errors.
An `add` or `edit` command is rejected if it would match another client's:
* Name, ignoring case and extra spaces. For example, `Alpha  Tester` (with two spaces) matches `Alpha Tester`.
Accented letters are stored in a standard Unicode form, so typing the same accent using a separate combining mark does not create a different name.
* Email address, ignoring case. For example, `alpha.tester@EXAMPLE.COM` matches `alpha.tester@example.com`.
The existing records remain unchanged when the command is rejected.

### Filtering clients by role, tag and requirements: `filter`
Shows only the clients who match a role, a tag, or any of their recorded requirements: preferred area, preferred housing type, budget and asking price.
* `ROLE` accepts `buyer`, `seller`, or `both`, ignoring case. Only one `r/` may be given.
* `r/buyer` shows buyers and clients marked `both`. `r/seller` shows sellers and clients marked `both`. `r/both` shows only clients marked `both`.
* A client with no role never matches a role.
* A tag matches a client's tag with the same name, ignoring case. The whole tag must match, so `t/urgent` does not match `urgently`.
* Repeat `t/` to give several tags. A client matches if they have **any** of them (OR).

* `AREA` is one of the [supported areas](#recording-a-clients-requirements-b-s-l-h), ignoring case. Repeat `l/` to give several areas. A client matches if **any** of their preferred areas is one of them (OR).
* `TYPE` is `HDB`, `Condo`, `EC` or `Landed`, ignoring case. Repeat `h/` to give several housing types. A client matches if **any** of their preferred housing types is one of them (OR).

* `BUDGET` is a price range written `MIN-MAX`, such as `b/500000-600000`, or a single price, such as `b/850000`. A client matches if their budget has at least one price in common with it, counting both ends. So `b/850000` shows every client whose budget includes $850,000, and `b/900000-1000000` shows every client whose budget overlaps that range. Only one `b/` may be given.

* `PRICE` is also a range written `MIN-MAX`, or a single price. A client matches if their asking price is within the range, counting both ends, so `s/850000` shows only clients asking exactly $850,000. Only one `s/` may be given.

* Prices follow the same rules as in `add` and `edit`: whole dollars from 1 to 1,000,000,000, with optional correctly placed commas. A range must be two prices joined by a hyphen, such as `500000-600000`, and one with a minimum above its maximum is rejected.
* A client with no preferred area, no preferred housing type, no budget or no asking price never matches a filter on that field.

* When several kinds of criteria are given, a client must match **all** of them (AND), but only one of the values within `t/`, `l/` or `h/` (OR). For example, `filter r/buyer l/Bedok h/HDB` shows buyers who want Bedok **and** an HDB flat.
* All parts are optional. `filter` with nothing after it shows every client.
* Text before the first prefix, such as `filter buyer`, is an error. An invalid role, tag, area, housing type or price also shows an error and leaves the displayed list as it was.
* The result line shows how many clients are displayed out of all clients in the book, e.g. `Showing 8 of 34 clients.`. The word `clients` is used even when the number is 1.
* `filter` replaces any filter or `find` search that is already active. It does not combine with it.
* `find` also replaces an active filter. Use `list` to clear the filter and show all clients.

* The filter stays active after `add`, `edit`, `delete`, `role`, `note` and `clear confirm`, so the displayed list can still be shorter than the whole book. Indexes in these commands refer to the displayed list.

* After `add`, `edit` or `role`, the changed client is checked against the active filter again. A client who no longer matches leaves the displayed list. For example, after `filter r/buyer`, `role 1 seller` removes client 1 from the list. In the same way, after `filter t/urgent`, `edit 1 t/weekend` removes client 1, because the client no longer has the `urgent` tag, and after `filter l/Bishan`, `edit 1 l/Orchard` removes client 1, because the client no longer wants Bishan.

* Among `add`, `edit` and `role`, only `add` can introduce a matching client to the filtered list, because `edit` and `role` can target only clients already displayed. For example, after `filter t/urgent`, adding a client tagged `urgent` shows them, and after `filter l/Bishan`, adding a client with `l/Bishan` shows them. A new client has no role, so after `filter r/buyer` they stay hidden; run `list` and give them a role, then filter again. `undo` and `redo` can also change which clients match the active filter.
* `delete` removes the client from the list, and `note` never changes which clients are shown, because a filter does not look at notes.
* `clear confirm` deletes every client, including the hidden ones, but the filter stays active. A client added afterwards stays hidden unless they match it, so run `list` to show everyone.
* `filter r/buyer` shows all buyers, including clients marked `both`.
* `filter t/urgent t/firsttime` shows clients tagged `urgent` or `firsttime`.

* `filter r/buyer t/urgent` shows buyers (including `both`) who are tagged `urgent`. On the sample clients this shows no clients (`Showing 0 of 5 clients.`), because the only `urgent` client, Nur Aisyah, is a seller.
* `filter r/both` shows only clients who are both a buyer and a seller.
* `filter l/Bishan l/Tampines` shows clients who want Bishan or Tampines. On the sample clients these are Alicia Tan and Cheryl Goh.
* `filter h/HDB` shows clients who want an HDB flat. On the sample clients these are Alicia Tan and Cheryl Goh.
* `filter l/Tampines h/EC` shows clients who want both Tampines and an executive condominium. On the sample clients this is only Cheryl Goh.
* `filter b/850000` shows clients whose budget includes $850,000. On the sample clients these are Alicia Tan ($800,000 to $1,200,000) and Cheryl Goh ($700,000 to $900,000).
* `filter b/1000000-1500000` shows clients whose budget overlaps $1,000,000 to $1,500,000. On the sample clients this is only Alicia Tan.
* `filter r/seller s/900000-1000000` shows sellers asking between $900,000 and $1,000,000. On the sample clients this is only Nur Aisyah, who is asking $950,000.
